canonical_output_and_pure_renderer.requirement: Every tool declares a mandatory canonical output as a JSON schema, returns one lossless JSON value, and a pure render(args, value) produces the model-facing content. Callers never parse prose for ids. A tool without an output schema fails registration.
canonical_output_and_pure_renderer.keel_implementation: Tool = name, description, params schema, output_schema, execute(), render(). Body returns data only; renderer builds text. Gate: tool without output schema fails registration.

model_facing_schema_field_restrictions.requirement: The model-facing schema is built by an explicit allowlist of name, description and parameters only. Execution callbacks, timeout, presenters and concurrency flags never leak into a request.
model_facing_schema_field_restrictions.keel_implementation: schemas() projects allowlisted fields; test that no callback/field leaks.

single_schema_vocabulary_and_unsupported.requirement: One schema vocabulary for params and outputs: scalars, arrays, objects with explicit additionalProperties, exact-one oneOf, enum/const, with inferred types. Argument mismatch yields INVALID_ARGS and invalid output yields INVALID_TOOL_OUTPUT. Unsupported JSON Schema keywords are rejected, never silently ignored.
single_schema_vocabulary_and_unsupported.keel_implementation: pydantic or a small schema compiler; reject unknown keywords at registration; same errors.

argument_snapshotting_and_immutability.requirement: Args are deep-frozen and snapshotted as lossless JSON before policy runs. Args cannot be rewritten later because history, audit, UI and execution must agree.
argument_snapshotting_and_immutability.keel_implementation: Immutable arg object; policy hooks return decisions, never modified args.

pre_execute_decision_model.requirement: Pre-execute decisions are allow, deny (reason plus optional structured error id), cancel, and ask (audited reason plus optional localized display reason). Only allowed-once proceeds; a missing approval channel or an agentless call is a denial.
pre_execute_decision_model.keel_implementation: Decision type in the permission gate (extends W3.x); display reason localized (M25). Approval seam fails closed: absence of an answerer yields unavailable (W3.12, add test).

monotonic_guards_deny_cannot_become_allo.requirement: Guards are monotonic: a final guard can only deny, never allow, so listener order cannot turn a denial into permission.
monotonic_guards_deny_cannot_become_allo.keel_implementation: guard() registry evaluated after all hooks; Tier 2 is implemented as guards.

post_execute_decisions_dlp_value_vs_disp.requirement: Post-execute decisions are accept, replace content or replace value (never both), attach context for the next request, or block with corrective feedback. Content replacement is presentation, not confidentiality: confidentiality requires block or replace-value.
post_execute_decisions_dlp_value_vs_disp.keel_implementation: Post hook API with the same rules; DLP (B3.8) uses block/replace-value. Conflict C-13: DLP tests assert the program/code-mode value is also hidden.

around_dispatch_timeout_and_cancellation.requirement: An around-dispatch wrapper for timeout/retry/metrics may replace but not remove the cancellation signal; the registry re-fuses the caller's signal so caller cancel always propagates.
around_dispatch_timeout_and_cancellation.keel_implementation: with_signal wrapper pattern; test that caller cancel always propagates. Cooperative per-tool timeout (timeoutMs / metadata timeout_s) asserts the tool forwards the cancel signal and reaches quiescence, is never sent to the model, and surfaces TOOL_TIMEOUT. For published long-running work, use a task-owned cancel signal after publishing the id, not the call's; cancellation of the call stops waiting but does not kill published work.

concurrency_classification_barriers_and_.requirement: Concurrency classifier isConcurrencySafe(args) is pure and only true opts in; omission, exception or invalid result is exclusive. Loop forms exclusive barriers and rolling-pool parallel runs; batch override maxParallelToolCalls.
concurrency_classification_barriers_and_.keel_implementation: Scheduler with barriers and a bounded pool; default exclusive.

deterministic_ordering_and_executor_cont.requirement: One outcome per input call in input order, including skipped calls on abort. The executor never settles while started work still runs; internal failure drains then rejects with a typed batch error preserving committed outcomes.

per_agent_restriction_intersection.requirement: Per-scope tool restriction allow/deny lists intersect; scoped registrations stay exempt. Deny-only admits later tools while an allow-list excludes them.
per_agent_restriction_intersection.keel_implementation: Agent frontmatter tools.allow/deny semantics exactly so (extends A1.12).

conditional_tool_activation.requirement: Conditional tool activation (when) is evaluated once per step with the captured model selection; the admitted set governs declarations and every call in that step, is disposed after the batch, and late results cannot restore removed tools.
conditional_tool_activation.keel_implementation: Per-step tool admission (e.g., vision tool only when the model supports images).

stable_error_codes.requirement: Stable error vocabulary: INVALID_ARGS, INVALID_TOOL_OUTPUT, UNKNOWN_TOOL, ABORTED, ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH, TOOL_TIMEOUT, APPROVAL_REJECTED/CANCELLED/UNAVAILABLE, TOOL_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE, plus UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT. Error info = name + code + optional raw reason kept durably but never in model-facing content.
stable_error_codes.keel_implementation: Error catalog (C10.2) with these codes; reason stored in log only. V28: AST scan generates typed-code list and troubleshooting pages; fail CI if a raised code is undocumented.

typed_expected_failures.requirement: Expected failures are typed errors with stable codes; successful domain outcomes (for example a non-zero exit) are values, not exceptions.
typed_expected_failures.keel_implementation: Rule in tool authoring guide; tests per tool.

turn_completion_and_deferred_context.requirement: conclude_turn() lets a successful tool end the turn and composites forward it only from authoritative nested success. defer_context() attaches context that the loop appends only after the result.
turn_completion_and_deferred_context.keel_implementation: Both on the tool run context.

typed_source_kind_for_injected_context.requirement: agent.inject() messages carry a typed source kind; old untyped wrappers are rejected at admission.
typed_source_kind_for_injected_context.keel_implementation: Source enum for injected context (supports taint).

long_running_background_lifecycle.requirement: Background start returns a typed handle {kind:'background', job_id}; the job spec has synchronous cancel and a non-rejecting done that settles after cleanup, plus an output source. After publishing the id, use a task-owned cancel signal, not the call's; cancellation of the call stops waiting but does not kill published work. job_kill, owner disposal and teardown own that lifetime.
long_running_background_lifecycle.keel_implementation: Matches Y1.7 + D3.7; make this the written lifecycle rule.

programmatic_tool_call_mode.requirement: Every visible tool is callable as await tools.name(args) with generated arg/output type maps. Calls re-enter the normal pipeline; success returns the canonical value after policy, failure rejects with a limited error (name, tool name, message only). Intermediate values are execution-local; only the outer run_code call crosses the output cap and spill pipeline. Model-direct calls to native names are denied while the PTC executor is selected and run_code is a reserved name.
programmatic_tool_call_mode.keel_implementation: Keel's Code Mode (Y1.1) follows these rules; design output_schema as a useful programmatic API. ptc-dispatch-log hook shortens only the durable log copy of a sub-call result; sub-call start/settle events store only ids, name and normalized args, never schemas/descriptions per sub-call. Executor-owned prompt sections registered and disposed with the executor (also MCP instruction blocks W4.11).

ui_presentation_purity_and_card_contract.requirement: Presenters are pure (present_call(args), present_result(args, result)), run on live stream and log replay, with no I/O, clock or session state. Malformed or old args fall back to a generic card and display must never crash a replay. Card kinds are generic, terminal, diff, search, read and web with defined fields and truncated/total so partial results are never shown as complete. Durable presentation_meta(args, value) is stored on the result; UI-only formatting stays out of model-visible output.
ui_presentation_purity_and_card_contract.keel_implementation: Renderer card components (Master 9.2) one per kind with states; meta field on tool result events; rule + review checklist; web client derives tool cards from raw events via a keyed slot per tool name, validates wire values locally, falls back to generic row, and imports no host code into the browser bundle.

contract_tests_and_verification.requirement: Permanent contract-regression specs for the agent loop; HMR-safety test for every registry (dispose the contributing scope, assert cleanup); table-driven tool conformance kit; fuzzer with random args/cancel points/injected failures; request-reconstruction byte-compare proving model-visible equals logged; smoke tests boot the shipped profile, send one prompt and check the world; guards proven red-green-revert; mock only the expensive/non-deterministic boundary.
contract_tests_and_verification.keel_implementation: tests/contract_regressions/ never deleted without owner note; per-registry unload test (V1/D1.2); release smoke (C13.4) + docs/postmortem/; make_bridge_harness() analog on the fixture model server (X9.1); conformance kit fails CI on any tool lacking conformance metadata.

subagents.finding: One activation API for local children and external executions; provider capability flags (agent_options, agent_preset, output_schema, depth_limit) validate start options before anything starts.
Result delivery policy: parent (notifies the model) vs caller (only returns result, e.g. workflows/code mode).

Agent names are 1-32 lowercase letters/digits/hyphens starting with a letter, not 'lead'; default agent-N, root lead, slash paths. Names are model-facing references, session ids are the authority; resolve grants no permission; no match fails AGENT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.
Child working directory chosen at admission (relative resolves against parent's current dir); local child keeps parent's original project; resumed child retains logged directory state.

Local child is a durable session with at most one live activation; manager owns identity/capacity reservation, input admission, cold resume, child-first disposal; structured-output capture closes input for that activation and resume does not inherit the schema.
Fork seeds the child with the parent's completed-turn prefix (contiguous, lossless, balanced steps); spawn starts fresh; inherits_parent_context is descriptive wording only.
External backends are providers (separate coding CLIs or protocol agents): one execution, no follow-ups, results to creator only while online.

Result object: final output = last non-empty assistant message; optional structured value validated; diagnostic limited to 4096 bytes and free of tool inputs, file contents, env values, credentials and raw protocol payloads; stop reason enum; child failure resolves with error, not exception.

Messaging within one tree: running target gets steer, absent target cold-resumes, sender identity rechecked, accepted messages never retracted. Two distinct source kinds: agent-message (relay) vs subagent-settled (runtime notice) so a child is never credited with words it did not write.
Interrupt authority: only the user or an exact live ancestor; fire-and-return; preserves unclaimed inbox, activation and descendants; claimed work not requeued; absent target is a no-op.
Whole-tree drain and wait-for-tree-work: idle members with parked input stay resident without delaying host completion.

Parent-owned catalog projection (membership at creation, no execution status); recursive list_descendants with parent id, depth, path and per-branch diagnostics (unsupported/corrupt/unavailable); cycles skipped; unreadable branch stops only that branch; historical children shown as unknown mode with no continuation rights.
Subagent model-route setting: default-off allowlist of provider/model routes, read live on each delegation; malformed/duplicate routes error.

User-authored message to a child from the UI with attachments (image parts via attachment store; model must accept images) and client time zone; cold resume at capacity rejects with typed delivery-unavailable.
Lifecycle events subagent/start, subagent/end (scoped to tree root), provider added/removed.

testing_policy.finding: HMR-safety test for every registry: dispose contributing scope, assert cleanup.
Permanent contract-regression specs for the agent loop.
Coverage gate philosophy: an uncovered line is often dead code to delete; line coverage necessary but never sufficient; environment-dependent files exempt locally but enforced on CI with the tool.

Performance benchmark gates as required PR checks: timed code on the plain runtime, never a transpiler; synthetic inputs enforce time, heap and scaling budgets; package-local perf files diagnostic only.

Snapshot scenarios: parent/child session files with version in filename agreeing with header; snapshot.yml declares profile/header class/recording policy/workspace facts; typed tokens keep identity relations; mutating scenarios compare full workspace.expected tree that record/refresh never rewrite; modes record/refresh; review every diff; CI read-only replay.
Fixtures omit sequence/time envelopes (replay synthesizes them); historical fixtures keep released representation with explicit format owners for migration coverage.
Browser snapshot lane: UI output compared in Chromium, model picker also in WebKit; replay-only in CI.

Test-process isolation: forked workers share ports/paths/namespaces/children; each test owns every resource through teardown; a spec passing only alone is a test defect; fork-exit diagnostics report PID/file/code/signal; flake-diagnosis workflow classifies probabilistic failures.
Smoke tests boot shipped profile, send one prompt and check the world; postmortems documented (postmortem/0001-*).

Mock only the expensive/non-deterministic boundary (model, network, clock); keep real tool registry/pipeline/persistence; recovery tests separate pre-chunk vs post-chunk failures; cover exhaustion, cancellation, policy composition, persistence, status, wire counts, idle timeouts, shipping loader composition.

Verify the world, not the agent's self-report: re-run command or re-read files externally; assert untouched files byte-identical; e2e tests create/dispose own resources even on failure; shared fixtures in plain helper modules.

Real-composition tests for product-visible plugins: boot test-only config through real loader, mock only external services, assert model-visible request/log or durable state; prove each guard fails when regression introduced (red-green-revert).
Test the published artifact entry path: run built entrypoints on plain runtime; assert missing config exits non-zero; singleton modules shared across bundles get a built-scope test.
Test resolution: tests resolve imports to source; built artifacts used only by explicit built-mode tests; subprocess tests use one shared launcher.
Every non-trivial model/protocol/human-visible change updates a keyless recorded-session scenario; new capability seams and lifecycle variants name every required test tier at plan time.

desktop_packaging_and_updates.finding: No listening port in the desktop app: backend is a bundled child; framed byte pipes carry requests and streaming responses with backpressure; Node IPC only lifecycle control; custom app:// protocol serves assets. Keel decision C-19 / V31: UDS/Windows named pipe for desktop, loopback+token for keel web and CLI.
Release identity: shell and backend always carry the same exact version; updater never updates one side alone.
Bundled runtime, never system runtime or package-manager state, and never the shell's own runtime for the backend.

Process-lifetime single-instance lock acquired before profile access; desktop exclusively owns its profile; CLI and desktop share product data but never executable packages, plugin activation, lockfiles or site-packages.

Transactional activation: staging install, full backend health check, replace active profile only after success; journal + one rollback profile; transaction lock records current owner including orphaned worker.

Seed store packaging: 16 deterministic uncompressed shards so differential updates reuse unchanged shards; offline install verification before shipping; measure disk use separately from installer size.

Update unit: shell + backend seed + runtime form one signed unit; update check 10 seconds after main window opens plus manual menu item; native confirmation; wait for in-flight check; verify, stop backend, install, reconcile next launch.
Plugin management window is a separate renderer receiving only structured operations: no filesystem, raw IPC, shell or arbitrary package-manager arguments.
Plugins with install-time lifecycle scripts rejected unless in a reviewed allowlist; prefer wheels only.
Shell copy localized from app locale, shared across menus, dialogs and plugin window, with English fallback; i18n gate checks desktop shell sources.
Isolated development home with disposable data/project/browser folders; debug ports by env; DevTools toggle; dev overrides ignored by packaged app.
Per-target build isolation under targets/<target>/ with shared download cache verified by name+hash; a target never consumes another's mutable state.
Release prerequisite env validation: app id format, reject malformed identities, incomplete credential sets; release --dry-run.
Packaging never receives upload credentials; target completion record written only after every build/sign step succeeds; build job has no deploy secrets.

Upload guard: require completion record matching environment/target/URL/version and check names, sizes, SHA-512 before reading credentials; immutable versioned artifacts first, channel metadata last with no-cache; never delete historical objects.
Test vs production update environments with distinct origins (beta feed vs stable).

Signing/notarization: hardened runtime + timestamp, deep strict signature check, DMG notarize/staple, Windows EV token with PIN never persisted. Excluded as paid in Keel; keep verification script pattern; use Ed25519 + checksums.
Linux is not a supported desktop release target in dsh, but Keel supports it (AppImage/DEB/RPM) by owner requirement.
Known-limitations section in desktop README: features disabled in desktop needing a server, shared vs separate state, release qualification needs production environment.

providers_credentials_model_ux.finding: Keys are write-only: UI receives redacted descriptor; settings store only a credential reference; masked preview uses identifier prefix plus 5 leading and 4 trailing characters only when at least 8 middle characters remain hidden (else all dots), counted in Unicode code points.

Saved key edit rules: no reveal/copy/partial edit; typing replaces whole key; Backspace/Delete stages whole-key removal applied on Apply; Cancel preserves; deletion-success/settings-failure warns deletion cannot be undone and offers retry; clearing a shared credential warns all features using the reference are affected.
Environment-credential hints: green env var detected, yellow none, 'unconfirmed' status read failed; detection never validates the credential; provider-managed credential files outside the check.

Model list follows provider's published list (loads on first need, background refresh about every 10 minutes while in use, built-in fallback); editing switches to pinned custom list; Restore defaults re-follows.

Third-party provider picker from installed catalog vs Custom model API form (permanent lowercase ID, base URL, protocol, credential, models); four protocols (OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini API); one protocol per provider; renaming = add new + delete old.

Model discovery: GET /models with searchable picker (existing pre-ticked, tick add, untick remove, Update list); configured models not listed stay; nothing saved until Save; failures fall back to manual entry; built-in provider always answered from catalog.

Model picker: selecting sets default for new sessions; a session keeps the model recorded in its own log; drag-to-reorder with keyboard up/down; deleted default provider blocks input with 'Select model'.

Per-model capability fields: input types (text, image), context window, max output tokens; route defaultInput fallback never removes catalog-known images; 'claims about your endpoint are not verified' warning; image-capable list clears image limits when image removed.

Reasoning-effort declarations per model with API value per level (off may send nothing), route default, picker choice saved as model default; thinking-format switch; models can drop levels; unsupported effort refused as UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT; Effort menu hidden when no levels.

Request-compatibility switches at route level with per-model field-by-field override; empty value refused, unknown name refused with valid-name list; each switch valid only for protocols declaring it.

Troubleshooting keyed by error code/symptom (missing credential, unknown model, 401 on discovery, gateway refuses all, only reasoning models fail, Effort menu absent, off doesn't stop thinking, image refused vs provider rejects, stale image in session log).
